# HMD.bio

> URL shortener and link analytics platform with a public REST API, owner
> dashboards, and an admin area. Base API URL: `https://hmd.bio/api/v1`.
> All API responses are JSON shaped as `{ success, data?, error?, statusCode }`
> unless a `?format=xml|jsonp|text` query param requests a different encoding.

HMD.bio lets anyone shorten a URL, and lets registered owners manage their
links, view click analytics, and integrate programmatically via a Bearer
API key. This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention:
a curated entry point for LLMs and AI agents, pointing at the canonical,
always-current sources below rather than duplicating them.

## API reference

- [OpenAPI 3 specification (JSON)](https://hmd.bio/api/docs): the complete,
  machine-readable contract for every endpoint under `/api/v1` — paths,
  methods, request/response schemas, auth requirements, rate-limit tiers,
  and error shapes. This is the authoritative source; prefer it over any
  natural-language description when generating API calls.
- [Interactive Swagger UI](https://hmd.bio/docs): human-browsable rendering
  of the same specification, useful for exploring endpoints interactively.
- [Full API reference (plain text)](https://hmd.bio/llms-full.txt): the
  complete inline expansion of the OpenAPI specification as a single
  markdown document, generated at request time so it can never drift from
  it — every endpoint, parameter, request/response schema, and error code
  with all `$ref` pointers already resolved. Fetch this one file to get the
  full contract without a second request.

## Authentication

- **Session cookie** — browser-driven requests from the dashboard only.
- **Bearer API key** — `Authorization: Bearer hmd_<key>`, issued via
  `POST /api/v1/auth/api-keys` (requires an existing session). Keys are
  shown in full exactly once at creation and stored hashed thereafter —
  there is no way to retrieve a lost key, only revoke and reissue.
- **API key scoping**: a key carries a `scope` of `read` or `write`, an
  optional `domains` restriction limiting it to specific hostnames the
  account owns, and an optional `expiresAt`. A read-only key is refused any
  request other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`. Keys issued before scoping
  existed carry none of these fields and behave as full access on every
  domain, never expiring. No key can create, list or revoke API keys, and no
  key carries its owner's administrator privileges.
- Public endpoints (`/shorten`, `/expand`, `/stats/[keyword]` for links the
  caller doesn't own) work without authentication. Endpoints that manage a
  specific account's links, exports, or API keys require a session or
  Bearer key.
- `401 Unauthorized` means no usable credential: none supplied, unrecognised,
  or expired. `403 Forbidden` means the credential is valid but not
  permitted: not the resource owner, a read-only key attempting a write, a
  key used on a domain it is not scoped to, or a key used on a session-only
  endpoint. A domain-restricted key addressing an existing link or domain
  outside its scope gets the ordinary `404`, not a `403`, so it cannot use
  the status code to discover that the resource exists.

## Rate limits

Sliding-window limits apply per caller, enforced via Upstash Redis with a
graceful in-memory fallback if Redis is unreachable (requests are never
left unlimited, nor do they fail, when the fallback is active):

- Public/unauthenticated: 30 requests/minute per IP
- Authenticated (session or API key): 100 requests/minute per account
- Per API key: 50 requests/minute, nested inside the account ceiling above

The per-key bucket sits inside the account bucket rather than beside it, so
several keys do not increase an account's throughput. It exists so that one
key cannot consume the whole allowance and starve the owner's dashboard or
another key. A session and a key on the same account count separately against
the inner bucket, but share the outer one.

Exceeding either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

## Core endpoints

- `POST /api/v1/shorten` — create a short link from a long URL. Public;
  requires a Cloudflare Turnstile token when the deployment has Turnstile
  configured, to prevent automated abuse.
- `GET /api/v1/expand?keyword=<keyword>` — resolve a short keyword to its
  destination URL without following the redirect. Public.
- `GET /api/v1/links` — list the authenticated caller's own links, with
  search, sort, and pagination. Requires auth.
- `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/links/{keyword}` — read, update, or delete a
  single owned link. Requires auth and ownership (or admin role).
- `GET /api/v1/stats/{keyword}` — per-link click analytics (referrers,
  countries, browsers, operating systems, time series). Requires ownership
  or admin role for links that have an owner.
- `GET /api/v1/user/stats` — aggregate totals across all of the caller's
  own links. Requires auth.
- `GET /api/v1/links/export` — streamed CSV export of the caller's owned
  links. Requires auth.
- `POST /api/v1/links/bulk` — bulk-create links from a JSON array (capped
  at 500 items per request). Requires auth.
- `GET /api/v1/links/{keyword}/qr` — QR code image for a short link.
- `POST /api/v1/links/{keyword}/unlock` — verify a password-protected
  link's password, rate-limited against brute force. Public.
- `DELETE /api/v1/links/{keyword}/clicks` — erase the click log for an owned
  link. `mode` must be given: `anonymise` clears the personal fields and
  keeps the anonymous analytics row, `delete` removes the records outright.
  `confirm` must echo `domain/keyword`. Requires auth and ownership, and a
  write-scoped key.

Full request/response schemas for all of the above, plus auth (`/signup`,
`/verify`, `/resend-verification`, `/email`), API key management
(`/auth/api-keys`), and admin-only endpoints (`/admin/users`,
`/admin/clicks`) are in the OpenAPI specification linked above — this file
intentionally does not restate schema details that would drift out of sync.

## Custom domains

Registered owners can point their own hostname at HMD.bio and create short
links on it instead of `hmd.bio`. A domain must be claimed and DNS-verified
before it can be used:

- `GET /api/v1/domains` — list the caller's own claimed domains, including
  each domain's live verification token. Requires auth.
- `POST /api/v1/domains` — claim a hostname the caller owns. Starts the
  domain in `pending_dns`. Capped per account (3 domains by default);
  exceeding the cap returns `403`.
- `GET /api/v1/domains/{hostname}` — fetch one of the caller's domains.
  Requires auth and ownership.
- `DELETE /api/v1/domains/{hostname}` — detach the hostname from the
  platform and delete the domain record. Links already created on it are
  kept, not deleted, but stop resolving; pass `?force=true` to remove a
  domain that still has links attached.
- `POST /api/v1/domains/{hostname}/verify` — check the DNS TXT record proving
  ownership, attach the hostname at the platform, and poll briefly for
  certificate issuance. Idempotent; rate-limited more strictly than the
  general authenticated tier, since each call walks a DNS zone the caller
  claims to own.

Once a domain reaches `active` status, links can be created on it by passing
`domain` (the bare hostname) to `POST /api/v1/shorten`, or per item to
`POST /api/v1/links/bulk` so a single import can span several domains.
Omitting `domain` on either endpoint always means the primary domain
(`hmd.bio`).

## Project background

- [README](https://github.com/hmddevs/hmd-bio/blob/main/README.md): full
  feature list, tech stack, project structure, environment variables, and
  local development setup.
- [Repository](https://github.com/hmddevs/hmd-bio): source code (Next.js
  16 App Router, TypeScript strict, MongoDB via Mongoose, Upstash Redis,
  NextAuth v5, Sentry).

## Privacy and data handling

Visitor IP addresses are never stored or logged in plaintext: they are
one-way hashed for analytics grouping, or AES-encrypted for admin-only
decryption. This is a hard invariant of the codebase, relevant if an agent
is asked to reason about what data this service retains about end users.

Retention of click data means anonymisation rather than deletion. As a click
ages, the personal fields on it (the encrypted visitor address, its IV, and
the user agent) are cleared, while the anonymous row (timestamp, country,
browser, operating system, referrer, keyword, domain) is kept, so the
analytics survive minimisation instead of being destroyed by it. Outright
deletion is available to any owner who prefers it, through
`DELETE /api/v1/links/{keyword}/clicks` with `mode: "delete"`, and is never
applied by default.
